items.title: Nvidia is trading almost completely independent of the broader semiconductor sector: The 3-month correlation between the semiconductor index, $SOX, and Nvidia, $NVDA, stands at just 0.03, the lowest among all index components. This is despite Nvidia having the largest market cap of all $SOX constituents. By comparison, Intel, $INTC, has a 3-month correlation with $SOX of above 0.90, the highest among all stocks in the index. Similarly, Taiwan Semiconductor, $TSM, and Micron, $MU, both have correlations with the index just below 0.90. Nvidia is no longer trading like a typical semiconductor stock.

items.content:
US consumers are planning to cut back on spending:

The proportion of consumers planning to spend more on restaurants, bars, and take out over the next 6 months fell -2 percentage points in August, to ~24.5%, the 2nd-lowest since September 2025.

US consumers expecting to spend more on health care services fell -3 percentage points in August, to ~19.5%, the lowest since September 2025.

Consumers are pulling back on spending plans.

items.title: The world's major central banks have finally unwound most of their pandemic-era balance sheet growth: The Federal Reserve’s total assets as a % of US GDP are down to 21%, the lowest percentage since the 2020 pandemic. By comparison, the peak was recorded in 2021 at ~37%. At the same time, European Central Bank assets as a % of Eurozone GDP fell below 40% for the first time since Q1 2020, from the ~65% peak in 2022. items.content:
The world's major central banks have finally unwound most of their pandemic-era balance sheet growth:

The Federal Reserve’s total assets as a % of US GDP are down to 21%, the lowest percentage since the 2020 pandemic.

By comparison, the peak was recorded in 2021 at ~37%.

At the same time, European Central Bank assets as a % of Eurozone GDP fell below 40% for the first time since Q1 2020, from the ~65% peak in 2022.

Total assets on the Bank of Japan’s balance sheet as a % of Japanese GDP are down to ~103%, their lowest since 2020, from the ~130% high in 2021.

The Bank of England’s assets are down to ~21% of UK GDP, the lowest since 2016, from the ~40% peak in 2021.

The pandemic-era central bank stimulus is largely gone.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Aug 27, 2026

items.title: Energy stocks have rarely seen this much hedge fund demand: Hedge funds bought the most global energy stocks in almost 4 years last week.
